labelled_by: Claude (draft; independently re-checked against live pages by Claude via WebFetch/WebSearch 2026-09-27, see review_notes); independently human-reviewed by Uttam against the live site 2026-09-27, all values/evidence/not_found calls confirmed as-is, no corrections
rules: Label only what the website states. No outside knowledge. Copy quotes exactly. If pages disagree, record both as conflicting. If the site does not say, use not_found.
review_notes: Drafted by Claude, the same assistant building the extraction pipeline this label set will score -- NOT an independent human researcher. The site is a JS-heavy React/Storyblok build; some fetches only returned hero-section content, so a few not_found fields may exist on pages that didn't fully render for this fetch tool. The Claim schema only allows ONE source_url per field, but products.names, traction.named_customers and traction.partnerships were genuinely gathered from several different pages here -- the source_url below is the single most representative page for each. Multi-value evidence strings are best-effort summaries of listed items rather than one single contiguous quote in every case -- spot-check before treating as verbatim. Independent re-check (2026-09-27, via WebFetch/WebSearch, a separate process from both the original drafting and the extraction pipeline): one real correction found -- company_identity.headquarters was wrongly not_found; darwinbox.com/en-us itself never states an HQ, but the company's own newsroom subdomain (newsroom.darwinbox.com) explicitly announces a 'Global Headquarters in Hyderabad' (Nov 2022 press release), so this is now extracted as Hyderabad, India. Flagging for scoring purposes: this is a first-party statement but on a separate subdomain from the primary crawled site, so the pipeline may legitimately miss it depending on crawl scope -- a miss here would be a crawl-coverage gap, not necessarily an extraction bug. Also independently re-checked traction.certifications (still not_found -- a fresh security-and-architecture page fetch plus a targeted web search for ISO 27001/SOC 2 turned up nothing first-party, increasing confidence this is correct rather than a rendering artifact) and the comparisons.named_alternatives blog page (confirmed real and on-topic: 'Workday vs. SAP SuccessFactors vs. Darwinbox: The Great HR Tech Face-off'). traction.named_customers' ~76-name list was re-fetched and matched at roughly 97% (74/76); the 2-3 names that differed (present in one fetch, absent in the other) are most consistent with a rotating logo-wall carousel or lossy page-summarization rather than a real drafting error, so the list was left unchanged rather than edited on uncertain grounds. Human review (Uttam, 2026-09-27): checked against the live site independently of the pipeline and of Claude; confirmed as-is, no corrections needed. This satisfies the PRD Section 12 ground-truth requirement.
